title: REIT、苦境下で「攻めの増資」　分配金成長に市場冷ややか
extracted_text:
不動産投資信託（REIT）の増資が相次いでいる。2026年に入って増資した8銘柄が調達した合計額は、25年通年の全体の調達額を上回った。REITの増資は物件取得に向けた「攻め」の戦略といえる。しかし市場の評価は芳しくはない。

「好ましくない増資が増えないかと心配している」。三井住友DSアセットマネジメントの倉島克彦シニアファンドマネージャーは浮かない表情を見せる。

市場で話題になった増資の一つがオフィス特化型の グローバル・ワン不動産投資法人 。3月25日に最大157億円を調達して都内と千葉市の2物件を取得すると発表した。運用会社のグローバル・アライアンス・リアルティの山崎弦IR部長は「長期的に分配金成長につながるとみて取得を決めた」と説明する。だが翌日の投資口価格（株価に相当）は5%下げた。

グローバル・ワンは26年9月期と27年3月期の1口あたり分配金予想を3200円としたが、売却益などを除いた1口あたり利益は27年3月期にかけ減少する。千葉市の物件の一部テナントでレントホリデー（契約期間のうち特定期間の賃料が免除される）条項があることなどが理由だが「都内の取得物件も築年数が古く、成長性や物件の質に疑問を持つ投資家は多かった」（東海東京インテリジェンス・ラボの中村貴司シニアREITアナリスト）との声も聞かれる。

同じく3月に増資で最大152億円を調達し沖縄のホテルなどを取得すると発表した Oneリート投資法人 も、翌日の投資口価格は6%安となった。中国地方の運用会社のファンドマネージャーは「取得したホテルは改修を要する。元々オフィス特化型のREITであり、本当に成長させられるとの確信を持てない」と話す。

今年に入り増資を発表した銘柄の投資口価格は総じてさえない。特に厳しい評価につながった事例で共通するのが、投資口価格が低迷する中での「ディスカウント増資」だ。NAV倍率（株式のPBR=株価純資産倍率=に相当）が1倍を切る状態で増資をすれば、投資口あたりの価値の希薄化や口数増加による需給の悪化が意識されやすい。

増資が相次ぐ背景には、REIT業界での積極的な物件取得による成長を目指す機運の高まりがある。25年は保有物件を売却し分配金に充てる動きが増え、東証REIT指数は年間で2割上昇した。NAV倍率が1倍を超える銘柄も増え「26年は増資による物件取得やそれに伴う分配金の増加期待もテーマ」（SMBC日興証券の鳥井裕史シニアアナリスト）と目されていた。

一方でNAV倍率が1倍未満で規模が比較的小さいREITは、保有物件を入れ替える余地が乏しい。増資で物件を取得し賃料収入を引き上げないと分配金を維持しにくい。岡三証券の並木幹郎シニアアナリストは「投資主価値を毀損しても、増資による規模拡大に頼らざるを得ない面がある」と話す。

REITは増資で魅力的な物件を取得し、物件の含み益を顕在化しつつ資産規模を拡大するのが本来の成長の姿だ。増資をしても市場の評価は下がらないREITもある。

例えば今年1月に増資で227億円を調達した 日本ビルファンド投資法人 は、スポンサーの 三井不動産 から中央区・日本橋のオフィスなどを取得。来期の1口あたり分配金・利益ともに今期から増加を見込む。公表後の投資口価格はおおむねプラス圏で推移した。

26年に入りREITの収益環境は厳しくなりつつある。国内長期金利の指標である新発10年物国債利回りは2.4%台に上昇。不動産価格も上昇が続いており「分配金成長につながる物件を取得する難易度は高まっている」とニッセイ基礎研究所の岩佐浩人上席研究員は指摘する。

3〜4月に決算を発表したREITでは分配金予想を見直すケースも相次いだ。 三菱地所物流リート投資法人 は4月に分配金の目標について、従来は年3.5%以上の成長としていたのを、2936円程度を当面維持すると変更した。一時的なテナントの退去や想定を上回る金利コストの増加が理由だ。

国内のREITは58本あるが、NAV倍率が1倍を上回るのはまだ少数派。苦境下の増資で投資口価格がかえって下がれば、市場での選別は加速する。みずほ信託銀行の小川剛宏氏は「投資口価格の低迷が続くREITは再編が選択肢になりやすい」と指摘する。増資ブームが業界の再編機運を高めるかもしれない。

（杵渕純平）

translated_text:
REIT capital increases are coming one after another. The total amount raised by the eight issues that conducted capital increases since the start of 2026 has exceeded the total amount raised throughout all of 2025. REIT capital increases can be seen as a "proactive" strategy for acquiring properties. However, market valuation is not favorable.

"We're worried about whether undesirable capital increases will keep happening." said Kashuhiko Kurashima, Senior Fund Manager at Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management, showing an uneasy expression.

One capital increase that became a topic of market discussion was for office-focused Global One Real Estate Investment Corporation. On March 25th, they announced plans to raise up to 15.7 billion yen and acquire two properties in Tokyo and Chiba City. Gen Yamazaki, IR Director at operating company Global Alliance Realty, explained, "We decided to acquire these properties because we expect them to contribute to long-term distribution growth." However, the investment unit price (equivalent to stock price) dropped 5% the next day.

Global One projected per-unit distributions of 3,200 yen for both the September 2026 and March 2027 periods, but earnings per unit excluding gains on sales will decrease toward March 2027. This is due to factors including rent holiday clauses (where rent is waived during specific periods within the contract term) at some tenants in the Chiba property. However, there were also comments like "Many investors had doubts about the growth potential and quality of the Tokyo acquisition property as well, given its age" (from Takashi Nakamura, Senior REIT Analyst at Tokyos Tokyo Intelligence Lab).

Also in March, One REIT Investment Corporation announced plans to raise up to 15.2 billion yen through a capital increase and acquire hotels in Okinawa and other properties. The next day, investment unit prices fell 6%. A fund manager at a Chugoku region operating company said, "The hotels acquired will require renovation. It was originally an office-focused REIT, so I'm not confident it can really grow them."

Since the start of the year, investment unit prices for issues announcing capital increases have generally been weak. What these particularly harshly evaluated cases have in common is "discounted capital increases" amid低迷ating investment unit prices. When capital increases are conducted while the NAV multiple (equivalent to PBR for stocks) is below 1x, dilution of per-unit investment value and worsening supply-demand from increased unit counts become major concerns.


The background to the series of capital increases is the rising momentum in the REIT industry to pursue growth through aggressive property acquisitions. In 2025, there was an increase in movements to sell properties in the portfolio and use the funds for distributions, with the TSE REIT Index rising 20% for the year. Issues with NAV multiples above 1x also increased, and "2026 was expected to see themes of property acquisitions through capital increases and the resulting distribution growth expectations" (from Hirofumi Torii, Senior Analyst at SMBC Nikko Securities).

On the other hand, REITs with NAV multiples below 1x and relatively small scales have little room to replace properties in their portfolios. Without acquiring properties through capital increases to raise rental income, it becomes difficult to maintain distributions. Analyst Mikiro Namiki from Okasan Securities said, "There are aspects where they have no choice but to rely on scale expansion through capital increases, even if it damages unitholder value."

The original growth path for REITs is to acquire attractive properties through capital increases, realize hidden gains on those properties, and expand asset scale. However, there are some REITs whose market evaluation does not decline even after capital increases.


For example, Japan Building Fund Investment Corporation raised 22.7 billion yen through a capital increase in January this year and acquired offices in Nihonbashi, Chuo-ku from sponsor Mitsui Fudosan. Both per-unit distributions and earnings for the next period are expected to increase from the current period. Investment unit prices have generally remained positive since the announcement.

Since the start of 2026, the REIT earnings environment has been becoming more severe. The yield on newly issued 10-year government bonds, the benchmark for long-term domestic interest rates, has risen to the 2.4% range. With real estate prices continuing to rise, "the difficulty of acquiring properties that will lead to distribution growth is increasing" noted Hiroto Iwasa, Senior Researcher at NLI Research Institute.

Among REITs announcing earnings reports in March and April, there have also been cases of revising distribution forecasts. In April, Mitsubishi Estate Logistics REIT Investment Corporation changed its distribution target from the previous assumption of maintaining growth of 3.5% or more annually to maintaining around 2,936 yen for the time being. This was due to temporary tenant departures and interest cost increases exceeding assumptions.

There are 58 REITs in Japan, but only a minority still have NAV multiples above 1x. If investment unit prices instead decline due to capital increases in these difficult conditions, selection in the market will accelerate. Takehiro Ogawa from Mizuho Trust Bank pointed out, "REITs with persistent low investment unit prices are likely to have restructuring as an option." The capital increase boom may accelerate restructuring momentum in the industry.

(Junpeki Kinebutchi)
title_en: REITs Pursue 'Aggressive Capital Raises' Amid Difficult Conditions; Market Remains Skeptical of Distribution Growth
